development plan and thereafter the construction activities will start on the spot.
Recommendation
1.24.10 The Committee recommends that “National Platform on Disaster Risk Reduction (NPDRR)
should be used to evolve a comprehensive mechanism for dealing with disasters by making it a
converging point for all institutions dealing with disasters. The Committee also recommends that
in the direction of strengthening the Disaster Risk Reduction, efforts should be made for bringing
the corporate social responsibility into this.
(Para 5.12.16 ibid)
Action Taken
1.24.11 The need to reduce the impact of disasters by means of systematic efforts has been
gaining recognition among Governments, worldwide. Disaster Risk Reduction is a cross cutting
development issue. It requires political and legal commitment, scientific knowledge, careful
development planning, application of technology, law enforcement, community participation, early
warning systems and effective disaster preparedness and response mechanism. There is a need to
foster an enabling environment for developing a culture of prevention and to enable concerted
measures to facilitate the integration of disaster management into development planning in various

32
sectors. It is therefore desirable that the Central and State Governments, stakeholders in the field
of disaster management and people representing different interests in the area should evolve a
participatory process of decision making in disaster management, which will not only strengthen
the disaster management structure and institutions all over the country but will also enhance the
federal structure of our polity. The functions of NPDRR are:
(i) To review the progress made in the field of disaster management from time to time.
(ii) To appraise the extent and manner in which the Disaster Management Policy has been
implemented by the Central and State Governments and other concerned agencies, and
to give appropriate advice in the matter.
(iii) To advise regarding coordination between the Central and State Governments/UT
Administrations, State Governments, local Governments and civil society organizations
for development of Disaster Risk Reduction.
(iv) To advice s uo-moto or on a reference made by the Central Government or any State
Government or a Union Territory Administration on any question pertaining to disaster
management.
(v) To review the Disaster Management Policy.
For the discharge of these functions, the Platform may:
(a) Call for information and comments from any government institution, any other
organization or an individual.
(b) Appoint committees or groups comprising members of the Platform and/or others as
may be necessary, and
(c) Commission through the Central Government or any other agency, studies, research
or reports on any specific issue requiring the attention of the Platform or its
committees or groups.
1.25 NATIONAL POPULATION REGISTER
Recommendation
1.25.1 The Committee observes that MHA projected the plan outlay during 2013-14 for Census
Surveys and Statistics including National Population Register (NPR) at 
R1783.16 crore which
was reduced to R1122.16 crore (excluding R220.00 crore earmarked for North Eastern Area)
which may affect the plan scheme of NPR substantially and other schemes to some extent. The
Committee, in view of this, recommends that the amount should be enhanced as per requirement
of MHA.
(Para 5.13.20 ibid)
Action Taken
1.25.2 One important component of the scheme of National Population Register (NPR) i.e.
issuance of Resident Identity Cards (RICs) to all usual residents of 18 years and above in the
country has been recommended by EFC. The proposal was placed before the Union Cabinet, which
has recommended the matter to a Group of Ministers (GoM). Two meetings of the GoM have been

33
held so far, but no decision has been taken yet. If the proposal is approved in this financial year,
additional budget provisions will be requested.
1.25.3 The next phase of the scheme of NPR, i.e. updating and maintenance of NPR Data base
is under submission and it has been directed to open NPR centres at each Tehsil for Direct Benefit
Transfer (DBT), initially in NPR States/UTs. Once approved, request for additional allocation of
funds will be made for this component of the scheme from the Ministry of Finance.
Recommendation
1.25.4 The Committee notes that the demographic data collection (in paper format) for creating
the NPR has been completed for the entire country along with House listing and Housing Census
in 2010. However, the Committee is constrained to observe that data digitalization process has not
yet been completed and as far as biometric enrolment and issuing of Aadhar Cards are concerned
the work is also at slow pace. Aadhaar card issuance and National Population Register would take
years to complete. Since, Aadhar card is linked with Direct Benefit Transfer Scheme, it should be
completed at a fast pace; otherwise the beneficiaries would not be able to avail their entitlements.
The Committee recommends that there should be some interlinkage between the Aadhar card and
the NPR otherwise it would prove to be duplication of whole exercise causing confusion in the
minds of common people about their utility and validity.
(Para 5.13.21 ibid)
Action Taken
1.25.5 The data digitalization of more than 117.36 crore records (97%) has been completed. The
work is in progress to complete the balance records.
1.25.6 The biometric enrolment for NPR has been completed for 14.52 crore persons. The steps
are being taken to expedite the work. However, the hindrance is the availability of UIDAI certified
operators which is a pre-requisite for biometric enrolment of any person. The problem is acute
especially in remote areas and the existing certified operators are not willing to travel to other
places.
1.25.7 Out of the 78 districts selected for DBT Phase II, the biometric enrolment is to be
undertaken by RGI in 33 districts. These 33 districts are spread over 11 States/UTs. The biometric
enrolment of all beneficiaries of various government schemes has been taken on priority in these
districts. At tehsil/taluk/block level, enrolment centres have been set-up in order to cover the
beneficiaries in the time bound manner apart from the normal camps which are organized in the
local areas.
1.25.8 To minimize the duplication of efforts between NPR and UIDAI, the Government has
decided that NPR enrolments will continue as envisaged but during the course of NPR biometric
enrolment, if a person indicates she/he is already enrolle d for Aadhaar, then the biometric data will
not be captured for NPR. Instead the Aadhaar number will be recorded in NPR and the biometric
data will be sourced from the UIDAI.
1.25.9 It has been also decided that once UIDAI completes major enrolment in an area, NPR would
follow and complete the enrolment in NPR.
1.25.10 Accordingly, the necessary software was finalized by UIDAI and the same has been
deployed in the field in all the NPR biometric camps since August, 2012, mainly in States/UTs

34
allotted to UIDAI. The capture of Aadhaar number/EID number is under progress, wherever any
resident indicates that she/he has been already enrolled under UIDAI.
Recommendation
1.25.11 The Committee is also apprehensive that refugees, foreigners and nationals of hostile
countries may try to be enrolled into NPR so that they could prove to be an Indian citizen. The
Government should look in this aspect seriously. The Committee is of the considered view that the
responsibility of NPR enrollment approval cannot be left to a local “patwari” particularly in those
areas where there are a large number of foreign nationals allegedly residing there. There must be
a high level foolproof mechanism in each district for scrutinizing and giving final approval and
cross checking. This is because the moment the National Population Register comes up, it will be
a legal document for claiming Indian citizenship and also avail related facilities.
(Para 5.13.22 ibid)
Action Taken
1.25.12 The sufficient steps have been taken to ensure the integrity of NPR database. The details
are as under:
(a) Primary collection of the data of every usual resident under NPR has been done by
house to house enumeration by duly authorized Government servants who have
signed each and every form.
(b) While collecting the data, the respondent has been cautioned that ‘providing any false
information would attract penalties under the Citizenship Rules 2003.’
(c) A signed declaration has been taken from the resident that “I declare that all the
information provided is true to be best of my knowledge and belief.” Thus, any false
information would invite penal consequences.
(d) All the filled-in NPR forms have been scanned and are available in electronic archive.
(e) The collected data has been digitized.
(f) The biometrics of the person in the NPR database being collected in the presence
of a Government servant, duly appointed for the purpose.
(g) The Government official(s) present at the NPR biometric camps check the digitized
database and confirm with the help of acknowledgement slip that the person
appearing at the biometric camp is the same person whose data was collected and
then take the biometrics.
(h) The person whose name is not found in the digitized database, would be included
in the NPR database by filling up new NPR form and only after the details provided
by the person has been verified by local registrar.
(i) After de-duplication by UIDAI and generation of Aadhaar number, the clean list of
usual residents along with photograph and Aadhaar number would be printed in the
form of Local Register of Usual Residents (LRUR) and provided to the local
authorities.
(j) LRUR would be published in the local areas for inviting objections and claims. The
LRUR would also be placed before the Gram Sabha/Ward Committee for social
vetting.

35
(k) Any claims and objections made with regard to entries in the LRUR should be
carefully enquired into by the Local Registrar appointed for this purpose.
(l) Provision for appeal against the order of the Local Registrar has been made in the
Rules. The Sub-district and District Registrars would carefully dispose these appeals
in a time bound manner.
(m) In sensitive areas, State/UT Government have been requested to take up additional
measures for verification and will be free to involve the local Police Stations or the
Village Chowkidars in the process of verification.
1.25.13 Therefore, at each and every stage, care has been taken to ensure not only that all genuine
usual residents are included in the NPR but also that the information provided is correct. All State/
UT Governments have also been requested to follow the above measures.
1.25.14 NPR is a register of usual residents which would contain citizens as well as non-citizens.
It is the first step towards the creation of a National Register of Indian Citizens (NRIC). After
completion of NPR, steps can be taken towards creation of NRIC as and when and wherever
desired.

Recommendation
1.26.1 The Committee understands that it is the constitutional duty of the Government of India to
promote Hindi language and it is duty of the Department of Official Language to promote/
encourage use of Hindi Language in all the Departments/Ministries of the country. The Committee
is of the view that all the documents of the Government of India should be made available
simultaneously both in Hindi and English.
(Para 5.14.13 ibid)

Departments to scrupulously follow the Official Language Act and Rules framed there under and

of Official Language Rules and other provisions of the Official Language Act, etc. The
recommendations of the Standing Committee have been circulated to all Ministries/ Departments for
compliance.
Recommendation
1.26.3 The Committee takes note of the fact that a Committee has been set-up recently to evaluate
present Hindi vocabulary and develop “saral” Hindi dictionary which could be used without any
difficulties for administrative and other purposes. The Committee desires that the evaluation
process done by the said Committee may be completed in a time bound manner.
(Para 5.14.14 ibid)

36
Action Taken
1.26.4 An eight member Expert Committee has been constituted for the purpose. The Committee
has been mandated to give its report in six months period. Two meetings of the Committee have
already been held on 25-5-2013 and 28-5-2013.
Recommendation
1.26.5 The Committee is constrained to observe that Ministry of Panchayti Raj, Department of
Chemical and Petrochemical, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research and Ministry of
Health and Family Welfare are not abiding by the provisions of Section 3(3) of the Official

upon these Departments/Ministries to follow the rules/acts in this regard strictly.
(Para 5.14.15 ibid)
Action Taken
1.26.6 All the Ministries/Departments have been issued instructions on 26.4.2013 to scrupulously
follow the provisions of Section 3(3) of the Official Language Act, 1963. The recommendation of
the Standing Committee have been circulated to the referred Ministries/Departments and they have

Recommendation
1.26.7 The Committee also recommends that the vacancies in various Departments/Ministries
should be filled up at the earliest. The Department of Official Language should pursue the matter
vigorously with Staff Selection Commission.
(Para 5.14.16 ibid)
Action Taken
1.26.8 V arious steps have been taken to fill up the various vacancies in different Ministries/
Departments at different levels. Departmental Promotion Committees (DPCs) have been held and
orders for promotion even on ad-hoc basis, wherever necessary were issued to fill up vacancies
in various grades of Central Secretariat Official Language Service(CSOLS) Cadre. Consequently,

Sr. Hindi translators, 61 Sr. Hindi Translators to the post of Assistant Director, 53 Assistant
Directors to the post of Deputy Director and 13 Deputy Directors to the post of Joint Director.
1.26.9 The vacancies at the feeder level of CSOLS i.e. Junior Hindi Translators (JHTs) are filled
up through Staff Selection Commission (SSC). SSC conducts yearly examination for recruitment
to the post of JHTs. In order to fill up the vacancies intimated by the Department to the SSC
expeditiously, matter was taken up with the Chairman, SSC through a D.O. letter from Secretary,
Deptt. of Official Language on 2.4.2013. DOL has since started receiving dossiers of selected
candidates of JHT Examination 2012. So far 10 dossiers of selected candidates have been received
in DOL from Zonal Offices of SSC at Bangalore and Raipur, which have been allocated to various
Ministries/Departments for appointing them on the vacant posts of JHT. On receipt of dossiers of
selected candidates from other Zones of SSC, allocations will be made to Ministries/Departments,

37
where vacancies exists. The Chairman, SSC has again been requested to instruct all Zonal Offices
to send dossiers of successful candidates expeditiously.

2.1 LEFT-WING EXTREMISM
Recommendation
2.1.1 The Committee also notes the death of several security forces personnel in LWE incidents
in 2012. In some cases, it was alleged that the personnel were posted in those areas without
adequate training and the casualties occurred due to non-observance of Standard Operating
Procedures (SOP). The committee feels that these issues need serious consideration and recommends
that the Government should provide adequate training to the personnel of Central Police Forces
as well as State police forces before sending them to LWE affected areas. The Committee also
recommends that these personnel should be equipped with all necessary modern weapons and
security gadgets and the required SOPs should be scrupulously followed by the forces.
(Para 3.6.17 of 169th Report)
Action Taken
2.1.1 ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ being State subjects, action with respect to maintenance of law
and order lies primarily in the domain of the State Governments concerned, who deal with the
various issues related to Left Wing Extremist (LWE) activities in the States. The Central
Government monitors the situation closely and supplements and coordinates their efforts in several
ways, inter-alia, including providing Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) to assist the State
Police Forces to deal with the LWE problem.
2.1.2 The CAPF battalions, prior to their induction in the LWE affected States, undergo Counter
Insurgency/pre-induction training at two stages. At the first stage, they undergo pre-induction
training of four weeks with the Army Infantry units and thereafter familiarization/orientation training
of 15 days under the respective State Police.
2.1.3 Besides, in order to strengthen the training inputs of the State Police Forces, the Central
Government has approved establishment of 21 Counter Insurgency and Anti-Terrorist (CIAT)
Schools in the States affected by insurgency and terrorism including Left Wing Extremism. Fifteen
such CIAT Schools have been established/are being established in the LWE affected States of
Bihar (3), Chhattisgarh (4), Jharkhand (4), Odisha (3) and West Bengal (1). The Central
Government also provides assistance to the State Governments in training of State Police Forces
through the Ministry of Defence, Central Police Organisations and Bureau of Police Research and
Development.
2.1.4 W ith regard to provision of modern weapons and gadgets, the Central Government is
providing financial assistance to the State Governments for modernization and upgradation of the
State Police Forces and their intelligence apparatus under the Scheme for Modernization of State
Police Forces (MPF Scheme).
41

42
2.1.5 The State Governments are advised from time-to-time to ensure observance of SOPs by the
security forces deployed in the LWE affected areas.
2.2 NORTH EAST
Recommendation
2.2.1 The Committee is concerned over the prevalence of insurgency in north-east with the
neighbouring countries of the region aiding and abetting ultra-groups in the region. The Committee
notes the large number of surrenders by the underground militants in recent period and is also
aware of the fact that the Government of India has initiated talks with NSC-IM and other militant
groups of the region and hopeful that it will yield desired results soon. The Committee feels that
neighbouring countries of the region should be diplomatically approached and negotiated at highest
level for not allowing their territories for carrying out anti-India activities by insurgent groups of
the region. The Committee understands that several schemes for infrastructural development scheme
are under implementation in the North-East. But the pace of the work is so less that its impact
is not much visible. This needs to change. The Committee is of the firm view that socio-economic
development and expansion of connectivity infrastructure in the North-eastern region only can
counter the ideological influence of the insurgent groups.
(Para 3.7.9 ibid)
Action Taken
2.2.2 The internal security and law and order situation in the North Eastern States, including
insurgencies and talks with various extremist outfits operating in the region as well as security
issues between Indo-Bangladesh and Indo-Myanmar are discussed at the highest level and these
issues are reviewed periodically.
2.3 TERRORISM IN J&K
Recommendation
2.3.1 The Committee notes the claim of the Ministry of Home Affairs that there has been decline
in terrorist violence and infiltration attempts by Pakistan based and aided militants in J&K and
quantum increase in flow of tourists visiting the Kashmir Valley. However, the Committee cautions
the Government from being complacent and to be vigilant constantly as the terrorist infrastructure
in Pakistan/PoK remains intact and infiltration attempts are still being made from across the
border.
(Para 3.8.7 ibid)
Action Taken
2.3.2 The Government has adopted various counter terrorist methods to neutralize the efforts and
capabilities of militants to disturb peace in the State. The Government has also encouraged policies
to mainstream the youth and discourage the local youth from joining militancy.

Recommendation
2.4.1 The Committee is of the view that “Orderly system” functional in Police forces is quite
discriminatory and reminiscent of British colonial era which affects the morale of the forces

personnel who are trained to become security personnel, however, employed as cooks, drivers,
attendants, etc. The Committee is of the view that this system should be abolished completely,
forthwith, as recommended by 6th Pay Commission. The Committee is also of the view that posts
of cooks, drivers, attendants, etc., if necessary, at the residences of senior officers of the forces
should be sanctioned separately.
(Para 4.1.9 ibid)

requirement/justification.
Recommendation

direction to all the heads of the Forces including the Delhi Police as well as police in UTs, for
not using any security personnel or police personnel for duties such as drivers, washermen, cooks,
attendants, peons, or for other personal use of the officers other than their regular security duties.

can follow.

have been regularized. The provision of work charge is guided by the CPWD manual and as per

working in Departments like PWD, electricity are governed under CPWD manual and accordingly

2.13 ANDAMAN & NICOBAR ISLANDS
Recommendation
2.13.1 The Committee takes note of the fact that the Government has sanctioned a project of
setting up of a Marina at Viper Island. Since, the matter pertains to the sentiment of the people
as the said Island has a historical value, the Committee recommends that the Ministry should
impress upon Ministry of Tourism and A&N Administration to shift this project to any other Island
of UT of Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
(Para 6.5.13 ibid)
Action Taken
2.13.2 The project was approved by the Ministry of Tourism after following due processes. The
Planning Commission had allocated an amount of 
R 7.5 crore as 50% subsidy under Tsunami
Rehabilitation Programme (TRP) for setting up of a 50 berth Marina in A & N Islands with a view
to revive Tourism in these islands which was badly affected by the Tsunami of December, 2004.
This Administration had taken up the project at Viper Island after a detailed feasibility study after
taking into consideration that Viper island is an uninhabited island which is techno-economically
ideal for setting up a Marina. Previously there was no activity/project on the island and hence it

50
was in a state of gross neglect. The entire island was not being utilised for any fruitful purpose
and was being littered due to stray cattle and waste swept inland by the sea.
2.13.3 It was felt that by setting up this project the island will be provided an overall facelift and
shall be maintained properly thereby attracting more tourists. Such a project would also result in
generating employment opportunities for local unemployed youth of these islands apart from
generating revenue for the Administration. By setting up a project of international standards the
islands would get the recognition and attention of all the visitors from world over as against the
earlier state of neglect. Further, the Administration is already taking necessary initiatives for a
holistic development plan for the heritage buildings/structures at Viper Island including preservation
of the structures and landscaping of the area.

Island and all the necessary clearances from Government of India had been taken i.e. EFC and SFC
meetings for clearing the project were held under the chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of
Tourism, Government of India after which the Concession Agreement was signed with the private
developer for executing the project in this island.
2.13.5 As regards project of Marina, the Administration had all along since the process of
conceptualization of the project, borne in mind that there should be no damage or disgrace to the
monuments and the sanctity/historical significance of the island should remain undisturbed. To this
end it was ensured that the Marina should be at a considerable distance from the existing jetty and
there should be a separate approach/jetty for the Marina visitors. The area for Marina would be
segregated and clearly earmarked causing no interference to the historical monuments.
2.13.6 The Andaman Nicobar Command had given a NOC for setting up a Yacht Marina in 2009.
However, this has been withdrawn recently. The Andaman Administration is exploring various
available alternatives and thus the project is being reviewed.
Recommendation

of ships by the A&N Administration.

Action Taken

necessary steps for finalizing the broad parameters of ships keeping in view the requirement of sea/
oceanic connectivity of Mainland-Island sector as well as Inter-Island sector of the UT of Andaman
and Nicobar Islands for the procurement of ships, including both construction of new ships as well

3.1 OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF DEMANDS FOR GRANTS
Recommendation
3.1.1 The Committee takes a serious view of the fact that a large quantum of unspent balances
are lying with State Governments under major schemes such as Modernization of State Police
Forces, Special Infrastructure Scheme in LWE affected States etc.. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Ministry should persuade lagging States/UTs to implement the Schemes/
Projects of the Ministry at a fast pace and if the attempts are still not yielding the desired results,
the State Governments may be asked to furnish the Utilization Certificates (UCs) at the earliest.
In case, UCs have become overdue, the amount may be asked to be surrendered or the same may
be adjusted while granting further allocation.
(Para 2.11 of 169
th Report)
Action Taken
3.1.2 The Scheme for Special Infrastructure (SIS) in Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected
States was approved for implementation during the Eleventh Plan period. The implementation
of the Scheme commenced in the year 2008-09. The works under SIS were sanctioned for
creating necessary infrastructure with a view to enable the security forces to effectively deal
with Left Wing Extremism. During the Eleventh Plan period from 2008-09 to 2011-12, a total
amount of 
R 445.82 crore was released under SIS to the 9 LWE affected States, against
which, Utilization Certificates for R 258.26 crore have been submitted by the 9 LWE affected
States so far.
3.1.3 The works were to be undertaken in remote and severely LWE affected areas. The Progress
of works under the Scheme has been slow due to serious security problems created by the
Maoists, reluctance of contractors to operate in these areas, difficulty in mobilization of material
and machinery resulting in slower utilization of funds. Further owing to changing situations in the
LWE theatre, the CAPFs are required to shift their bases often, which necessitate change of works
approved under SIS leading to delays.
3.1.4 The MHA has been pursuing at all levels for Utilization Certificates and physical and
financial progress report by sending letters/reminders regularly to the State Governments
concerned.
3.1.5 The Ministry of Home Affairs has been taking up the issue of unspent balances lying with
States under the Scheme for Modernization of State Police Forces with the concerned State
Governments from time to time. In various meetings held in MHA, the Ministry has impressed upon
the State Governments to speed up the pace of implementation of the Action Plan approved under
the Scheme and utilize the funds released by the Ministry of Home Affairs for the purpose,
expeditiously.
51

52
3.1.6 The State Governments are requested to furnish Utilization Certificates (UCs) which are due
for rendition to Ministry of Home Affairs timely. The UCs furnished by the State Governments
form the basis for release of grants-in-aid to States under the Scheme in subsequent years. While
processing release of funds to States under the Scheme, the amount of unspent balances lying with
the States for which the UCs have become overdue, is deducted/adjusted by the Ministry of Home
Affairs from the allocations made to the concerned State and the remaining amount is released to
the State.
3.1.7 There is a provision in the Scheme which allows that funds which could not be released
to States due to unspent balances of previous financial years, as on 31
st December of the Financial
Year, may be pooled up and released to better performing States which have a faster pace of
expenditure.
FURTHER OBSERV ATION
3.1.8 The Committee is constrained to express its displeasure that almost half of the
amount allocated during Eleventh Five Year Plan under the Special Infrastructure Scheme
to the State Governments is lying unspent. The Committee understands that
implementation of development projects/schemes in LWE areas is a challenge for the
Government but partial completion of projects would frustrate the very purpose of the
allocations. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of Home
Affairs should impress upon the State Governments to put all out efforts for optimal
utilization of earmarked allocations in furtherance of execution of developmental projects/
schemes and submit the utilization certificate in time.
3.2 NATIONAL INVESTIGATION AGENCY
Recommendation
3.2.1 The Committee is constrained to express its displeasure that NIA, a premier investigating
agency, entrusted with the responsibilities to investigate and prosecute offences affecting the
sovereignty, security and integrity of India is working without required manpower and essential
facilities such as vehicles and the officers of the Agency are forced to perform their duties using
private taxies. The Committee, therefore, strongly, recommends that all the vacancies in NIA must
be filled up at the earliest and the Agency should be provided with all needed infrastructural and
logistic support. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Finance should come forward with
positive attitude and provide requisite fund for the three proposed regional offices of the NIA at
the RE stage.
(Para 3.9.6 ibid)
Action Taken
3.2.2 During the year 2012, the sanction for creation/operationalisation of 04 new branches of
NIA at Guwahati, Lucknow, Mumbai and Kochi with 265 posts has been issued.
3.2.3 Sincere efforts are being made for filling up the IT and Legal posts by writing to the Chief
Secretaries, Director Generals of Police and Directorate of Prosecution of various states for
nominating willing and competent officials for deputation to NIA.
3.2.4 As Recruitment Rules for some of posts were not finalized, NIA were authorized to fill the
posts without consultation with UPSC vide MHA order dated 8.01.2010. This exemption expired in
January, 2013 and the matter regarding extension of this exemption for a further period of one year
has been taken up with DoPT at the level of Home Secretary. However, despite these concessions

53
NIA has not been able to fill up all the posts due to non receipt of sufficient nominations. To meet
this deficiency, MHA has allowed NIA to fill up the posts on hiring basis/outsourcing, as a
temporary measure. Such sanction have been issued for 10 IT staff, 05 Data Entry Operator, 04
Housekeeping staff. It has also been decided to provide the personnel to NIA on attachment basis
for which the posts have been circulated to the various CAPFs for sending the nominations.
3.2.5 W ith regard to funds, additionality will be projected to Ministry of Finance/Planning
Commission at Supplementary stage/Revised Estimate stage.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.2.6 The Committee expresses its displeasure over the non framing of Recruitment Rules
for some of the posts. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Recruitment Rules must
be finalised without further delay. The Committee further recommends that the
Government should expedite filling up of 265 sanctioned posts for operationalisation of four
new branches of NIA at Guwahati, Lucknow, Mumbai and Kochi. Besides, inducting state

Committee is also of the view that various CAPFs should be advised to send nominations
of suitable officials to fill up the required posts. The Committee reiterates its
recommendation that Ministry of Finance should take necessary steps to provide requisite
fund for the three proposed regional offices of the NIA at the RE stage.
3.3 NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE GRID (NATGRID)
Recommendation
3.3.1 The Committee is constrained to express its deep displeasure over dilly-dallying attitude of
the Government in regard to creation of infrastructure of NATGRID. The very proposal of setting
up of NATGRID is still at nascent stage even after a lapse of two years. The Committee
understands that delay in construction of Data centre building of NATGRID would create hurdles
in accomplishing the set objective of the organization. The delay is unacceptable and the project
should pick up pace. The Committee observes that there is no seriousness on the part of Central
Government and, therefore, recommends that the Home Minister or the Cabinet Secretary should
have a meeting with all the concerned Ministries to clear procedural bottlenecks and this project
should take off on immediate basis without any further time and cost overruns.
(Para 3.10.6 ibid)
Action Taken
3.3.2 The NATGRID is conceived to be the frame-work which will enable visibility of a big
picture and of events beyond the horizon by collating disjoined pieces of information that exist in
different parts of the environment and stitching them into one view. It will leverage information
technology to access, collate, analyse, correlate, predict and provide speedy dissemination.
3.3.3 Planning Commission has accorded its “in Principle” approval to the project on 08.07.2012,
as a ‘Central Plan Scheme’ under Ministry of Home Affairs from 2011-12. Cabinet Committee on
Security has approved the ‘Detailed Project Report’ (DPR) for an amount of 
R1002.97 crores on
14.06.2012 for Implementation of Foundation, Horizon-I and some elements of Horizon II of the
project. Accordingly, work on the Foundation and Horizon-I has already commenced, and the
current stage of the project is detailed below:–
(i) The detailed organization structure, staffing Plan, role and responsibilities and other
elements of the NATGRID personnel have been prepared and sent to the Department

54
of Personnel and Training (DoP&T). Comments of the DoP&T have been received and
the proposal is being sent to the Ministry of Finance for approval after which their
recruitment will commence.
(ii) An interim arrangement to induct a team of about 30 select positions has also begun.
(iii) Land has been allotted to NATGRID for Construction of Data Centre (DC & BCP) at
New Delhi and for Disaster Recovery Centre (DR) at Bengaluru.
(iv) As per the approval of the Cabinet Project Management Consultants (PMC) are being
hired to design the various RFPs for System Integrators for implementation of
NATGRID solutions. Also, as per the Cabinet approval, information related to Banks
and Financial Institutions are to be provided through the Financial Intelligence Unit
(FIU), for which the Detailed Project Report shall be prepared.
(v) The construction work of data centre building has been entrusted to National
Building Construction Corporation (NBCC) on a turn-key basis. An EFC proposal for
construction of Data Centre Building has been prepared and sent to the Ministry of
Finance for appraisal. As per the EFC Memo, the projected timeline for
commissioning the Datacentre and Disaster Recovery is about 30 calendar months
after approval of the Cabinet. Thus, NATGRID would become fully functional after
these facilities are ready for launching of The full-fledged NATGRID solution.
However, preliminary support to User Agencies can commence well before that with
several pilot Project.
3.3.4 As regards Standing Committee’s recommendation that meeting be convened at the level of
Home Minister or Cabinet Secretary to clear procedural bottlenecks, the matter is under
consideration for further action.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.3.5 The Committee is not convinced with the explanation and expresses its anguish over
inordinate delay in creation of infrastructure of NATGRID. Despite “in Principle” approval
by the Planning Commission in July, 2012 for the project and approval of Cabinet
Committee on Security of the ‘Detailed Project Report’ (DPR), the ground work is yet to

bottlenecks should be cleared at the earliest so that the creation of infrastructure for
NATGRID should be expedited.
3.4 CRIME AND CRIMINAL TRACKING NETWORK AND SYSTEMS (CCTNS)
Recommendation
3.4.1 The Committee understands that Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and System
(CCTNS) project would go a long way in tracking criminals and investigation of criminal cases,
besides strengthening citizen based service delivery system. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Government should complete this project within stipulated time frame for its actual
operationalisation. The Committee is of the strong opinion that the project should not suffer for
want of funds, and therefore, further recommends that enhanced allocation may be made for
CCTNS project during the current financial year, if necessary. The Committee also desires that the
physical target of project implementation by August, 2013 should be achieved.
(Para 3.13.5 ibid)

55
Action Taken
3.4.2 The prime reason attributed to downsizing is less releases to States/UTs under Grants-in-
Aid. States/UTs have not been released funds because of low utilization of funds already allocated
to them. The Budget had been downsized from the initial Budget Estimates of v 400 crores in year
2012-13 to the Revised Estimates of 
R 85 crores.
3.4.3 The project implementation schedule of Crime and Criminal Tracking Network Systems
(CCTNS) project to be implemented in the Eleventh plan (2007-12) was proposed for four years
(2008-12). The schedule for four years was primarily based on a rationale that project activities
shall be undertaken by diverse stakeholders and would be successfully completed within the
proposed time. The various reasons for the delay are as follows:
● The CCTNS project is based on the principle of “Bundle of Services” wherein a
“System Integrator”(SI) would provide turnkey implementation of all the services
which will constitute implementation of a project in a State/UT. There has been
considerable delay in signing of the SI contract at State/UT level.
● The CCTNS project was conceptualized with a view to leverage the existing IT
infrastructure and network being developed under the other schemes of Department of
Electronics and Information Technology (DeitY) such as SWAN (State Wide Area
Network), SDC (State Data Centre), NSDG (National Service Delivery Gateway) etc.
However, there is a considerable delay in the completion of the above mentioned
schemes when aligned with the proposed implementation schedule of CCTNS project
from the year 2008-12.
● The project initiation activities of CCTNS project in terms of project conceptualization,
preparation of State Plans, preparation of project guidelines, templates, RFPs and other
key project guidance documents which should have been ready in the year 2008-09 for
timely initiation of the project before the approval of CCEA note, were mostly complete
only by the end of the financial year of 2009-10.
● The Core Application Software (CAS) of CCTNS project should have been completed
for initiation of rollout in the year 2009-10 as envisaged in the CCEA note. However
the Software Development Agency (SDA) at the Central level was selected only by
June, 2010 after a bid process which started in August, 2009. The latest build of CAS
has been released to States/UTs only in Dec, 2012.
3.4.4 The work of Project implementation is in full swing across the country. Also, provided that
the Project Implementation deadline is 30th June/31st August, 2013, all States/UTs shall need to
make pending payments to System Integrator, State Project Management Unit (SPMU) and BSNL
in the next few months itself, hence the Ministry shall require more funds to be sanctioned/released
to States/UTs who inturn shall make the respective payments.
Current Status of the Project implementation and action taken to ensure progress as per timelines:
3.4.5 All States/UTs have been given a mandate to finish the CCTNS Project Implementation by
30th June or 31st August, 2013. Various actions are being taken to facilitate the State/UTs to
achieve the timelines and also to help them utilize the funds released to them. Some such steps
are:–
● Regular meetings at Home Secretary /AS/JS levels are being held with State Nodal
officers/System Integrators(SIs) /SPMUs and BSNL to monitor and push the progress
in each respect.

56
● Regular visits are being made by National Crime Research Bureau (NCRB) and CPMU
to review the progress in various States/UTs. NCRB and MHA has been intervening in
any matter that States/SIs or SPMUs need help with.
● In order to facilitate faster implementation by the SIs, payment terms are being revised
for SIs, which shall ensure that SIs have the needed cash flow and hence can
continue to work to meet the prescribed timelines.
3.4.6 Below paragraphs detail the Status of implementation of the project:
(a) Selection of System Integrator (SI) by all the States/UTs: 31 State/UTs have till date
signed their respective System Integrator (SI) contracts and 1 State has issued Letters
of Intent to the respective SI. The resources have been deployed by the SIs at the
States/UTs and work is in full swing.
(b) Selection of State Project Management Units (SPMU) by all the States/UTs: 31 States/
UTs have signed contracts with their respective SPMU. The resources have been

(c) Network Connectivity: BSNL has signed the Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with 27

May 2013 and BSNL is currently working on providing network connectivity at the

(d) Capacity Building: District Training Centre (DTC), Regional training Centre (RTC),

(e) Financial Aspects: Total funds of 
R 446.54 crores have been released to States/UTs as

3.5 BORDER MANAGEMENT
Recommendation
3.5.1 The Committee understands the hurdles coming in the way of fencing, construction of roads
etc. due to difficulties in terms of acquisition of land, difficult terrain, non-cooperation from
bordering countries etc. The Committee is of the view that the Government should sort out all these
bottlenecks at the earliest and complete remaining works of fencing and flood lighting as targeted
in a given timeframe. The Committee recommends that the Government should diplomatically
approach and negotiate with the Bangladesh Government for border fencing within 150 yards along
Indo-Bangla Border. An early decision may be taken in the matter.
(Para 3.14.22 ibid)

57
Action Taken
3.5.2 Indo-Bangladesh Border Road passing through Dampa Tiger Reserve (DTR), Mizoram: A
stretch of about 59 km. (BP-2305 to 2313) for construction of border roads along Indo-Bangladesh
Border, falls within the territory of DTR, Mamit district in Mizoram is pending for Forest/
Environment clearance. MoEF clearance is being expedited by the State Government with the
concerned State Wild Life Board (SWLB) and National Board for Wild Life (NBWL) keeping in
view the importance of national security. Their response is awaited in the matter.
3.5.3 Land acquisition:- Execution of works covering about 95 km of border length under
Phase-II project has been adversely affected due to pending land acquisition (LA). This includes
79.58 km. in West Bengal, 11.31 km. in Tripura and 4.11 km. in Mizoram. Although, land
acquisition issues are being regularly monitored/reviewed by the MHA, the problem has persisted
over the years and, given heightened public sensitivities, States have been making slow progress.
The executing agencies viz. CPWD, EPIL and NBCC have been advised to expedite the same in
coordination with the concerned State Governments and BSF.
3.5.4 Delay on account of public protests:- In Meghalaya, construction works under Phase-II
project, in a stretch of about 133 km., has remained suspended for long due to protest by the
Coordination Committee on International Border (CCIB) of Meghalaya. Following continuous
persuasion by MHA, matter in respect of 62.55 km has been sorted out in November, 2011 and
work resumed. With further persuasion with the State Government, stretches of 7 km more have
been sorted out subsequently. Issues including land acquisition for the balance stretches of
63.45 km. are still to be resolved before work commences. A.D.O. letter from JS(BM) has been
addressed to the Chief Secretary, Meghalaya, with the request to convene a meeting to sort out
the above-mentioned issues.
3.5.5 Issues of Fencing within 150 yards of the international borders:- Fencing is generally
constructed beyond 150 yards of the IBB. However, due to existence of population within 150
yards of the IBB and also topographical constraints, it has sometimes been necessary to undertake
fencing within 150 yards of the IBB. This activity has been objected to by Bangladesh. India has
been trying to persuade Bangladesh Government through meetings at different levels  viz.  Home
Secretary, Foreign Secretary, DG/ BSF that the proposed fencing is for the mutual benefit of both
the countries and will help in curbing illegal cross-border activities.
3.5.6 Earlier there were 46 such identified priority patches, and subsequently 185 priority patches
were identified by BSF. It is also stated that both the Border Guarding Forces of the countries
undertake joint survey of these patches. Accordingly, the total priority patches comes to 231. Till
now 129 have been jointly been surveyed by BSF and BGB for fencing within 150 yards from IB.
Patches which need not to be covered are 92 and 10 patches are still required to be jointly
surveyed by BSF and BGB.
Measures adopted by the Government to sort out the problems related to land acquisition, public
protest and 150 yards
3.5.7 The problems of land acquisition and public protest in Meghalaya and Tripura are being
settled by active participation of Land Revenue department of the concerned State Government,
executing agency and BSF. The role of Coordination Committee on International Border (CCIB) is
also important in this case.
3.5.8 MoEF clearance is being expedited by the State Government with the concerned State Wild
Life Board (SWLB) and National Board for Wild Life (NBWL) keeping in view the importance of
national security.

58
3.5.9 The balance border works like fencing, roads and floodlighting are under progress and
are likely to be completed in the given time-frame. The work is targeted to be completed by
March, 2014.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.5.10 The Committee is of the strong view that the concerns for national security cannot
wait too long and even compromise on account of forest/environment clearance. Therefore,

th Report on the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2012 has

th Lok Sabha) of the Committee on Empowerment of

3.11 REHABILITATION OF REPATRIATES FROM SRI LANKA
Recommendation
3.11.1 The Committee finds that Sri Lankan Government is not abiding by the Commitment made
in the agreement on the issue of repatriation of Sri Lanka Refugees. The Committee understands that
this is very sensitive issue where two countries with ethnic overlapping are involved and the
rehabilitation process would take a long time. The Committee observes that 99,469 refugees have been
repatriated back to Sri Lanka upto March, 1995, and thereafter, there is no organized repatriation.
In view of the large influx of Tamil refugees, the Committee is of the view that the approach of the
Government of India should be to see that the influx of refugees should be discouraged and they
should be rehabilitated in their own homeland of Sri Lanka. The Committee in this regard notes that
as a follow up action decided in the Inter-ministerial meeting, a joint inter-ministerial delegation was
to visit camps in Tamil Nadu in January-February, 2012, but its visit is yet to be materialized. The
Committee understands that other course of actions are to be followed up on the findings of the
delegation. This reflects non-seriousness of the Government in redressing the problem. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the course of action as decided in the inter-ministerial meeting held by
Ministry of External Affairs be pursued in the right earnest. The Government should try to prevail
upon the Sri Lankan Government to create conditions conducive for their return.
(Para 5.8.15 ibid)
Action Taken
3.11.2 The Ministry has already requested the State Government of Tamil Nadu as well as the
Ministry of External Affairs to finalize the programme and date for visit of joint inter-ministerial
delegation to the refugee camps in Tamil Nadu to assess the desire of Sri Lankan refugees in India
to return to Sri Lanka and ascertaining the kind of facilitation they expect for this. The Ministry
of External Affairs has also been requested to follow up the action as decided in the inter-ministerial
meeting.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.11.3 The Committee is not at all satisfied with the reply. In spite of its recommendation,
no visit of Joint-inter-Ministerial delegation to the camps, till date, has taken place. The
Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation and strongly desires that all necessary
steps be taken to mitigate the sufferings of Tamil refugees.

3.13 DISASTER MANAGEMENT
Recommendation
3.13.1 The Committee in its 161
st report had observed that a specialized force like National

65
Disaster Response Force (NDRF) having 10 battalions only, for entire country, will not serve the
purpose and recommended for raising more battalions of this force. The Ministry in its Action
Taken Reply had mentioned that a draft Cabinet Note for raising of two Additional NDRF
battalions by conversion of two SSB battalions has been prepared by NDRF and the total battalions
of NDRF will be raised to 12. The Committee in its 165th Report on ATR of the Government then
observed that conversion of two SSB battalions into NDRF will not be right approach as it would
affect working of SSB and recommended to the Government to explore other sources to raise
additional battalions of NDRF . The Ministry in its written reply has mentioned that 10 Battalions
of National Disaster Response Force have been constituted for the purpose of specialist response
to disasters and are located at 10 strategic places across India. The Committee is constrained to
observe that the Government has done very little in compliance with the recommendations of the
Committee. The Committee reiterates its recommendation that the Government should raise more
Battalions of NDRF for responding to disasters.
(Para 5.12.10 ibid)
Action Taken
3.13.2 The Ministry of Home Affairs has taken the decision of raising two new NDRF battalions
converted from SSB battalions in Sept. 2009. To provide prompt response to the South-Western
area of the country, it was decided by the Ministry to station the new NDRF battalion in Karnataka
to take care of parts of Kerala and Karnataka. For providing response to the North-Eastern part
of the country, one NDRF battalion has already been deployed at Guwahati. On requisition of the
State Government of Assam, NDRF battalion deployed at Guwahati provides response to the Upper
Assam during any disaster situation.
3.13.3 Though NDRF is a specialized and well-equipped Force, it is a fact that it is not meant to
the first responder in a disaster. The task of first response is always discharged by the official
machinery of the concerned State Government/UT administration. It is therefore our endeavour to
encourage State Government to develop their own State Disaster Response Force (SDRF). It is also
necessary for the State Governments to pool in their resources, from Home Guards, Civil Defence,
Fire Services, State Red Cross, Nav Yuvak Kendra, National Cadet Corps and National Social
Service V olunteers so that the Disaster Management apparatus is kept in a constant and high state
of preparedness.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.13.4 The Committee is not satisfied with the vague reply submitted by the Government
with regard to raising more battalions of NDRF for responding to disasters. The Committee
reiterates that there should not be conversion of SSB battalions or battalions of other para-
military forces as it would badly affect the working of SSB or other para-military forces.
The Committee is of the considered view that there should be other sources for creating
additional battalions of NDRF.

Recommendation
4.6.1 The Committee is constrained to expresses its displeasure to find that there is a shortage of
1093 IPS officers in the country which shows lack of action on the part of the Government. The
role of IPS officers in the administration of the country is well known and need not be emphasized.
The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Government should explore the possibility
to overcome this shortage by filling up the vacancies on promotion from State Police Service
Officers and also on special recruitment drive from Central Police Forces.
(Para 4.12.4 ibid)
Action Taken
4.6.2 In this regard, as on 01.01.2013 there are 1453 posts under promotion quota of IPS
offices, out of which 1063 officers are in position. Hence, there are 390 vacant posts under
promotion quota. In order to fill these vacancies, the Ministry of Home Affairs has already
determined 274 vacancies in 23 segments/cadres. The concerned State Governments as well as the
UPSC have already been intimated about these vacancies and the MHA has requested the concerned
State Governments and the UPSC to initiate the process of convening the Selection Committee
Meetings to fill these vacant posts. In some of the States seniority list as under litigation and the
process of induction could not be processed further.
4.6.3 As far as, the special recruitment drive from Central Police Forces is concerned, MHA in
consultation with UPSC has already conducted the first Limited Competitive Examination-2012.
However, the LCE Rules were quashed by the Hon’ble Central Administrative Tribunal Guwahati
Bench in O.A. No. 112/2012 filed by Shri S. Deka. The same was challenged by MHA before
Hon’ble High Court of Guwahati. Hon’ble High Court has set aside the orders of the CAT. There
are some cases pending in various CATs related to LCE. A decision on declaring the final result
will be taken in consultation with UPSC.
4.7 TELEPHONE TAPPING
Recommendation
4.7.1 The Committee takes note of the incidents of unauthorized telephone tapping and getting
Call Data Records (CDR) of some prominent individuals including politicians in recent past for
ulterior motive. There were also alleged reports of the country’ s elite intelligence agencies involved.
In view of this, the Committee recommends that such incidents should not occur in future and
directs the Ministry of Home Affairs to issue a strict guideline in this regard. The Committee is
of the view that there should be a mandatory provision that before getting CDR or telephone
tapping of a sitting Member of Parliament, permission of the Presiding Officer of the concerned
House should be solicited. Similarly, in the case of other political leaders, the Chief of the Party
may be informed before taking any such action.
(Para 5.9.6 ibid)
Action Taken
4.7.2 In order to have an effective legal regime for seeing Call Data Records (CDR), a new Rule
419 B under the Indian Telegraph Rules, 1951 for calling message related information is under
consideration of DoT/MHA. Issue of seeking CDR or telephone tapping of a sitting Member of
Parliament or other political leaders with permission of the Presiding Officer of the concerned
House or Chief of the Party, as the case may be, is under consideration.

72
 4.8 JAMMU AND KASHMIR
Recommendation
4.8.1 The Committee is aware of the pitiable condition of the J&K migrants and note that much
progress has not been made in the implementation of Prime Minister Package except in respect of
employment and transit accommodation. The Committee notes that the migrants failed to reach any
consensus amongst themselves about the return to the Valley. The Committee understands that the
Government has not been able to create conducive environment in the valley so that the migrants
feel safe to return to the valley. The Committee, therefore, feels that the Government should create
a safe environment involving local communities in the valley so that these migrants could return.
The Committee notes that the Prime Minister Package framed in 2008 needs some changes and the
revision is already underway. The Committee recommends that the revised package may be finalized
at the earliest.
(Para 5.11.13 ibid)
Action Taken
4.8.2 A view for return to the Valley is to be taken by the migrants, in terms of the provision
of the PM’s package 2008. As per the information available with the Government, the security
situation in the Valley has improved considerably. Though the State Government has proposed a
revised package for return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants, the financial implication for the
same is awaited from the State Government The revised package will be processed on receipt of
financial implications from the State Government.
4.9 LAKSHADWEEP (51st IR Battalion)
Recommendation
4.9.1 The Committee is pleased to note that a decision regarding detachment allowance on the
line of armed forces has been taken up. The Committee hopes that the matter would be seriously
pursued by the MHA with the Finance Ministry, so that final decision of the Government is taken
up on the issue.
(Para 6.2.6 ibid)
Action Taken
4.9.2 Details of pattern/parity/ration of the detachment allowance given in other CPMFs personnel
are being collected by UT of Lakshadweep. On receipt of the information, they will take up the
matter with competent authority.

Committee on Security of the ‘Detailed Project Report’ (DPR), the ground work is yet to

of

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of
Development of North Eastern Region on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and
Seventieth Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2013-14) of the Ministry. The One
Hundred Seventieth Report was presented to Rajya Sabha/laid on the Table of Lok Sabha, on the
25
th/26th April, 2013.
2. Action Taken Notes as received from the Ministry of DoNER in respect of the
recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Seventieth Report have been categorized as
follows:
Chapter–I: The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the
Government: Para Nos. 2.3.4, 2.3.7, 2.4.8, 2.4.9, 2.5.3, 2.6.6, 2.7.15, 2.7.16, 2.8.14,
2.8.15, 2.9.8, 2.9.17, 2.9.18, 2.10.6, 2.10.7, 2.11.6, 2.13.6, 2.13.9, 2.14.5, 3.2.4, 3.3.9,
3.3.14, 3.6.4, 3.6.5, 3.7.6, 3.8.3, 3.9.6, 3.9.7, 3.10.5, 3.10.7, 3.10.9 and 3.11.1 (of One
Hundred and Seventieth Report) Total recommendations – 32
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its thirty one
recommendations as mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
Chapter–II: The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to
pursue in view of the Government’s replies: Para Nos. 2.3.11, 2.12.5, 2.15.4, 3.1.2, 3.3.11
and 3.7.5 ( ibid) Total recommendations – 6
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and,
therefore, does not want to pursue the recommendations further.
Chapter–III: The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee is not
satisfied with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos. 2.3.6, 2.4.4, 3.3.7, 3.3.8, 3.4.9, 3.4.10,
3.6.7, 3.8.4, 3.9.8 and 3.10.6 (ibid) Total recommendations – 10
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its
recommendations contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should furnish
convincing action taken steps in respect of those recommendations.
Chapter IV : Nil
3. The details of the ATNs have been analyzed in the succeeding chapters.

2
CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH
HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
1.1 PROJECTED DEMAND IN THE BUDGET 2013-14
Recomendation
1.1.1 The Committee notes with concern that against the projected Demand of Ministry of DoNER
for the year 2013-14 of R 3614.91 crore only R 2006.00 crore has been approved. The Committee
wonders as to also how the Ministry will make up for such a huge deficit of
R 1608.91 crore and recommends the Ministry to take up the matter with the Planning Commission
and Ministry of Finance to enhance allocation at the RE Stage so that originally envisaged course
of actions are undertaken with enhanced allocation. This will, however, depend on the expenditure
pattern.
(Para 2.3.4 of 170th Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 The observations/recommendations of the Committee have been noted. The matter regarding
enhancement of allocation, depending on the expenditure pattern, will be taken up with the Planning
Commission and Ministry of Finance at the RE Stage.
FURTHER OBSERV ATION
1.1.3 The Committee would like to be apprised of the outcome of efforts made by Ministry
of DoNER regarding enhancement of allocation at RE stage of 2013-14.
1.2 NORTH EASTERN CLIMATE CHANGE ADOPTION-PROJECT
Recomendation
1.2.1 The Committee feels that the Ministry should have presented its case before the Planning
Commission more strongly to get its proposed 12th Plan outlays approved. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry should improve its absorption capacities so that it can demand more
funds for various projects. The Committee finds that adverse effects of climate change in NE
Region can be seen from decreasing rain fall in the region and increasing melting of glaciers. In
view of the Committee, the NE Region has become highly vulnerable to the consequences of
climate change and the adaptation as well as mitigation projects are the need of the hour. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that Planning Commission should also consider allocating funds
for North East Climate Change Adaptation Project.
(Para 2.3.7 ibid)
Action Taken
1.2.2 It is submitted that North Eastern Climate Change Adaptation Project (Financial Co-operation)
is being considered by Government of India under Indo-German Co-operation in five North Eastern
2

3
States, namely, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Mizoram and Sikkim. The overall project cost is
Euro 99.7 million and the project duration is 7 years. The financing mechanism requires
reimbursement method of payment, i.e., the upfront payment for the project activities have to be
made by Government of India through Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region securing
about 6% contribution from the States and 5% contribution from the State communities, both
purely in kinds. At the time of budget estimate proposals, the project was not ready for
implementation. Certain critical issues like creation of Regional Society and its location and funding
mechanisms were not finalised. Therefore, it was decided to present the budget requirement to the
Planning Commission after Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) approves the proposal. It is
noteworthy that ‘No objection’ from all concerned line Ministries has been obtained including from
Planning Commission. At this stage, Planning Commission has been requested for ‘in principle’
approval and budget allocation for the project following which steps shall be taken to obtain final
approval of Government of India.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.2.3 The Committee notes the reply and desires that the Planning Commission should
give ‘in principle’ approval at the earliest.
1.3 NORTH-EASTERN COUNCIL
Recomendation
1.3.1 The Committee, while noting that the success of NEC efforts depends heavily on the
cooperation from the State Governments, feels that the Council should evolve an incentive structure
for better performance so that performing States could be motivated to do better and non-
performing States may be made to feel that they may loose on account of non-performance.
(Para 2.4.8 ibid)
Action Taken
1.3.2 The suggestion of the Committee has been noted and steps would be taken to evolve an
incentive structure for better performance of States.
Recomendation
1.3.3 The Committee desires that the Council must also evolve mechanisms to complete the
projects on time despite very short working season in the North East Region as one cannot alter
the geographical cycles. The Committee recommends that NEC may conduct a comparative study
on how projects are completed in other countries of similar climatic conditions suffering from
similar handicaps. The Committee also notes unavailability of raw material as well as limited
capacity of contractors and executing agencies. The Committee feels that the Government should
come forward to address those deficiencies affecting execution of the projects in NER by
augmenting supply of raw material and assistance to the executing agencies by providing soft loans
to them.
(Para 2.4.9 ibid)
Action Taken
1.3.4 The suggestion of the Committee have been noted and steps would be taken on the
direction of the Committee to address the deficiencies affecting execution of projects in NER.

4
1.4 CONSTRUCTION/IMPROVEMENT OF ROADS OF ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE
Recomendation
1.4.1 The Committee is dismayed over the fact that the Mahadev-Tolloi-Pfutsero road still
remains incomplete even after close to a decade. The Committee is aware that the State
Government of Manipur had earlier refused to implement the project and the same was handed over
to BRO for completion last year itself. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the
construction of road be completed this year without any excuses. The Committee further
recommends that more projects should be identified to be taken up under the scheme.
(Para 2.5.3 ibid)
Action Taken
1.4.2 The comments of the Committee have been noted. The Standing Finance Committee (SFC)
chaired by Secretary, DoNER, in its meeting held on 3
rd October, 2013, inter alia , considered the
Revised Estimates submitted for this project by BRO. The SFC has recommended revised project
cost of 
R 98.02 crore (original cost: R 74.12 crore) and projected date of completion as
March, 2015. During the SFC meeting it was reiterated that the revised cost and date of completion
should be adhered by the BRO and further request for the revision of cost/extension of date for
completion in respect of this project shall not be considered by the NEC.
FURTHER OBSERV ATIONS
1.4.3 The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the work relating to Mahadev-Tolloi-
Pfutsero road will be completed by March 2015.
1.5 NON PLAN LOANS TO NORTH EASTERN HANDICRAFTS AND HANDLOOMS
DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (NEHHDC)
Recomendation
1.5.1 The Committee understands the crucial role of NEHHDC in promotion and development of
handicrafts and handloom in the NER and therefore, feels that its revival need to be done. The
Committee notes with concern that the earmarked allocation is not sufficient as it falls short of
R6.50 crore to implement Revival Plan of the Corporation, which stands cleared by Cabinet
Committee of Economic Affairs (CCEA). The Committee urges upon the Finance Ministry to allocate
the required amount so that NEHHDC may make turn around in the year 2013-14 as per its
projections.
(Para 2.6.6 ibid)
Action Taken
1.5.2 Ministry of Finance has already been approached to release additionality of 
R 6.00 crore during
the current fiscal. Ministry of Finance has advised Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
to pose the additionality in the Supplementary Demand for Grants. This Ministry will be asking for the
additionality of R 6 crore in the ensuing supplementaries, as advised by Ministry of Finance.
1.6 LOAN TO NORTH EASTERN REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING
CORPORATION (NERAMAC)
Recomendation
1.6.1 Given its mandate of encouraging food processing units in NER and providing basic
infrastructure for marketing of agricultural and allied products, the allocation of 
R 2.00 crore for

5
BE 2013-14 to NERAMAC is too low for carrying out its activities. The Committee notes that the
allocation has remained the same for the years 2011-12 RE and 2012-13 BE. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Working Capital of the organization may be increased as per its
additional requirement of Rs.6.00 crore keeping in mind that the corporation is a profit making
organization with huge potential for growth.
(Para 2.7.15 ibid)
Recomendation
1.6.2 The Committee notes that Fruit Juice Concentration Plant at Nalkata, Tripura, which was
able to absorb the entire production of pineapple grown in the area and was able to provide better
price to farmers, has outlived its life and requires renovation and restructuring. The Committee is
disappointed to note that despite its recommendation made in 145th Report (Demands for Grants
2010-11) for early implementation of modernizing and restructuring of the plant, the same has still
not been done. Similarly, a Cashew Processing Unit at Agartala in Tripura , which was able to
absorb a major portion of the cashew nut grown in Tripura, has also been closed due to strictures
from Pollution Control Board. The Committee has been informed that a proposal to relocate the
plant is pending with Government of Tripura. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that
the requirement of working capital may be provided immediately for increasing its activities
manifold thereby making huge impact on the farmers and producers of the region.
(Para 2.7.16 ibid)
Action taken [Para Nos. 2.7.15 and 2.7.16]
1.6.3 W ith the issue of Ministry of Finance Office Memorandum No. 7(2)/E. Coord./2013 dated
18
th September, 2013, a cut of 10% has been imposed on Non-Plan expenditure during the current
fiscal. Notwithstanding this, the Ministry will take up the issue of enhanced allocation with Ministry
of Finance for BE 2014-15.
1.7 NORTH EASTERN DEVELOPMENT FINANCE CORPORATION LIMITED (NEDFi)
Recomendation
1.7.1 North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited (NEDFi) is an extremely
important Institution of the NER which provides term finance to industry, agro-horticulture based
industries and infrastructure along with services to the small entrepreneurs of the region. The
Committee has been informed that the Corporation is projecting internal generation of around
R 300 Crore, market borrowing of R 90 Crore and soft loan of R 60 Crore from the Ministry
of DoNER during the financial year 2013-14. The Committee notes that though the Corporation
has a target of 25-30 per cent growth on year-on-year basis but it has scaled down its
disbursement target from 
R 485.00 crore during the financial year 2012-13 to R 450 Crore during
the financial year 2013-14 due to resource constraints. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that adequate fund may be provided to NEDFi at RE stage to carry out its activities as
projected.
(Para 2.8.14 ibid)
1.7.2 The Committee is given to understand that the corporation has fund requirement of
R5184 crore during the Twelfth Five Year Plan to meet the projected sanctions of R 6410.00 crore
and disbursement of  R 4690.00 crore. The corporation has further requested for interest-free loan
to the tune of R 1000.00 crore from the Government during Twelfth Five Year Plan. Keeping in
view the pivotal role of NEDFi, the Committee reiterates its recommendation made in its
162nd Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Ministry that the Government should

6
consider interest-free loan to the tune of R 1000.00 crore for ensuring NEDFi to meet its financial
and physical targets during the Twelfth Five Year Plan.
(Para 2.8.15 ibid)
Action Taken
1.7.3 Financial assistance is provided by the Government of India to North Eastern Development
Finance Corporation Limited (NEDFi) in the form of interest-free loan. Against proposed Twelfth
Plan outlay of 
R 350 crore for loan to NEDFi, this Ministry have been informed allocation of R
300 crore only. Also against Central Plan outlay of R 6506.60 crore proposed by Ministry for
Twelfth Plan, Planning Commission have informed allocation of R 955 crore only. Hence, Ministry
is unable to increase amount of interest free loan being provided to NEDFi. As advised by the
Parliamentary Standing Committee matter is being taken up for enhancing interest free loans to
NEDFi during 2013-14 to R 200.00 crore at RE Stage and twelfth Plan allocation to R 1000.00
crore.
FURTHER OBSERV ATION
1.7.4 The Committee notes the efforts made by the Ministry of DoNER and desires to be
apprised of the result in this regard.
1.8 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
Recomendation
1.8.1 The Committee is highly dismayed and extremely dissatisfied with the abysmal rate of
completion of projects under the scheme. The Committee was given similar excuses for non-
performance during the consideration of Demands for Grants (2012-13) wherein it noted in its
recommendation given in 162nd Report. The same set of excuses are again being given this year
like delay in tendering process, delay in transfer of funds to implementing agencies, delay in
utilization of funds and timely non-submission of correct and proper documents by State
Governments etc. The Committee feels that nothing has changed on ground except for tall promises
to rectify the situation. The Committee strongly recommends that the various steps mooted by the
Ministry should be implemented immediately so that marked improvement gets visible in real terms
by next financial year.
(Para 2.9.8 ibid)
Action Taken
1.8.2 The observations of the DR-PSC have been noted. Projects under NLCPR Scheme are
implemented by State Governments. To expedite the completion of projects various review meetings
have been held at the level of Secretary, DoNER and Chief Secretaries of the States have been
asked to review the progress of projects on quarterly basis. Progress of implementation of projects
under the scheme shall be monitored vigorously further with the State Governments. During
2013-14 upto September, 2013, State Governments reported completion of 54 projects at a cost
of 
R. 514.29 crore.
FURTHER OBSERV ATION
1.8.3 The Committee views that intensive monitoring of progress of implementation of
projects under NLCPR scheme would definitely result in achievement of set targets.

7
1.9 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
Recomendation
1.9.1 The Committee notes the gap between grants released during 2009-2012 and Utilisation
Certificates submitted for the period by the States. While grants to the tune R 2376.58 crore were
released during the period, utilization certificates for only R 1838.78 crore have been submitted by
the States. This kind of non-submission of UCs creates hurdles in the way of fresh allocation from
the Pool for projects which, in turn, delays the completion of projects causing time and cost
overruns. The Committee urges upon the State Governments concerned to submit Utilization
Certificates on time so that funds could be released on time and delays could be avoided.
(Para 2.9.17 of 170th Report)
Action Taken
1.9.2 During 2012-13 State Governments submitted utilization certificates of R 753.22 crore and
during 2013-14 upto 30.09.2013 State Governments submitted utilization certificates of another
R 413.15 crore. A letter has been issued to the State Governments of North Eastern Region conveying the
concerns of Parliamentary Standing Committee and requesting to expedite the utilization certificates
for timely completion of projects. Matter was also reviewed during review meetings with the State
Governments
FURTHER OBSERV ATION
1.9.3 The Committee notes the action taken by the Ministry of DoNER and desires that the
efforts may continue in the right earnest.
1.10 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
Recomendation
1.10.1 The Committee notes that despite achieving budgetary targets and quarterly expenditure
targets, Grants from Central Pool of Resources for North Eastern Region were significantly reduced
at the RE stage 2012-13 by the Finance Ministry. The Committee recommends that the Grants
should be appropriately restored so that physical targets could be met.
(Para 2.9.18 ibid)
Action Taken
1.10.2 Recommendations of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee have been
conveyed to the Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission with a request to restore the grants.
1.11 BODOLAND TERRITORIAL COUNCIL (BTC)
Recomendation
1.11.1 The Committee notes that under the BTC Package of 
R. 500 crore, 42 projects at approved

1.21 INLAND WATER CONNECTIVITY
Recomendation
1.21.1 The Committee understands the importance of Inland Waterways as an alternative to other
modes of transport which are found lacking in many parts of the region. Inland waterways has
huge potential which can also be used to supplement the existing routes on land. Waterways are
the cheapest mode of transport anywhere in the world. In Western European countries, about 40
per cent of the cargo movement is by waterways. The world’ s average is about 8 per cent, whereas
in India it is less than 1 per cent. The Committee is surprised to find that in the National Water
Policy, navigation comes almost towards the end on the list of priority. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that navigation in NER should find priority as it is not only an economical mode of
transport but also eco-friendly and there is immense scope for improvement in the field of Inland
Waterways in NER. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of Shipping
along with Ministry of Water Resources should pursue all the projects vigorously in close
coordination with the Ministry of DoNER. The Committee also recommends that fund constraints
should not come in the way of the implementation of projects. The Committee also recommends that
Inland Water Transport projects in Tripura, Meghalaya and Mizoram which are at various stages
of planning may be expedited and finalised.
(Para 3.8.3 ibid)
